route: 1 (per-item published mean and SD, paper Table 8) + full 120-permutation uniqueness check
evidence: Route 1 (per-item published descriptives), decisive. Paper Table 8 'Descriptive statistics for exercise motivation items (N = 45)' (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0345759.t008, an image table) publishes mean and SD for each intrinsic item; live irw_fetch reproduces both for all five: IM1 4.111/0.885 vs 4.11/0.885, IM2 4.200/0.815 vs 4.20/0.815, IM3 4.356/0.830 vs 4.36/0.830, IM4 4.200/0.842 vs 4.20/0.842, IM5 4.244/0.830 vs 4.24/0.830; largest |dMean| 0.0044, largest |dSD| 0.00036; subscale average observed 4.2222 vs published 4.22. The five published (mean, SD) pairs are mutually distinct -- 2 and 4 tie at mean 4.20 but differ in SD (0.815 vs 0.842), 3 and 5 tie at SD 0.830 but differ in mean (4.36 vs 4.24) -- so the route distinguishes EVERY item from EVERY other item. All 120 permutations of the five Table 1 wordings were scored on the joint (mean, SD) residual: identity 0.00481, best other 0.03181, identity the unique minimum. What this does NOT establish: the option_text-to-resp axis, which is not verified by this route at all; that axis needs no inference, because S2 Data ships IM1..IM5 as label strings alongside IM1_num..IM5_num as integers and the per-item crosstab is one-to-one with zero off-diagonal cells (IM1 disagree/2 n=2, ordinary/3 n=9, agree/4 n=16, strongly agree/5 n=18), matching the S1 File codebook's stated '1-5 (strongly disagree=1 ... strongly agree=5)'.

route: per-item descriptive statistics (1); response-frequency matching (9) for the option axis
evidence: Route 1 (per-item descriptive statistics), on the live table, N=45, against Liang & Wang (2026) Table 8 'Descriptive statistics for exercise motivation items (N = 45)', an image table fetched from the PLOS figure endpoint and read directly. Live (M, SD) vs published: im_1 4.1111/0.8848 vs 4.11/0.885; im_2 4.2000/0.8146 vs 4.20/0.815; im_3 4.3556/0.8300 vs 4.36/0.830; im_4 4.2000/0.8421 vs 4.20/0.842; im_5 4.2444/0.8300 vs 4.24/0.830. Largest |dM| = 0.0044, largest |dSD| = 0.0004. The assignment is ONE-TO-ONE and every item is distinguished from every other: matching each live item against all five published rows at tolerance 0.02 on M and 0.005 on SD returns exactly one candidate per item, and the correct one. Neither statistic alone would suffice -- published means tie at 4.20 (items 2 and 4) and published SDs tie at 0.830 (items 3 and 5) -- so the pair is what pins them. Corroboration: subscale average observed 4.2222 vs published 4.22; Cronbach's alpha observed 0.9140 vs published 0.914 for the intrinsic subscale (extrinsic is 0.883), which also confirms this is the intrinsic block. Code-to-source tie checked separately: live im_k == S2 Data IM{k}_num for 45/45 respondents, k=1..5, exact and one-to-one. Option axis settled by route 9, not by this route: S2 Data's paired label/integer columns crosstab one-to-one with zero off-diagonal cells for all five items (e.g. im_3 disagree/2 n=1, ordinary/3 n=7, agree/4 n=12, strongly agree/5 n=25). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the administered Chinese wording, which is unpublished -- the English shipped is the authors' rendering, not a verbatim transcript of what respondents read; and the item-2 clause-order discrepancy between Table 1 and Table 8, which is a printing difference in the source, not something the statistics can resolve. Neither bears on which code carries which item.
